what: 250 labels driven through the REAL batch UI in a browser — CSV + 250 image files handed to the page's own file input, so the client path runs end to end: prepareImage (downscale + deskew) per image, 250 object URLs, filename pairing, streaming table.
why: docs/rubric.md P3 was previously evidenced only by scripts/measure.ts, which posts to /api/check from node and therefore skips everything the browser does per row. An audit correctly noted that no 250-row run through the actual UI was evidenced. This is that run.
wall_source: the app's own footer figure (performance.now around the run)

bucket_after_run.note: Every row lands in Needs review because the batch exceeds BOLD_GATE_EAGER_MAX (60), so the bold measurement pass is opt-in and had not been run. 228 rows were offered under 'Check bold type'. This is the documented, deliberate behaviour — a row whose bold was never examined must not show a green tick — but it is also the real cost of that choice, and on the brief's headline 250-label case it means 'review exceptions only' starts as 'review everything'. Recorded here rather than left as a claim in prose.

row_verdicts_sampled: each sampled row read '4 matched • 2 not required', i.e. the field comparisons themselves succeeded
caveats: The browser pane running this was not composited for part of the run. Timers throttle in that state, so treat 146.5s as an upper bound on wall-clock rather than a tuned figure; the count-and-error results are unaffected because they are fetch-driven.
Images are 12 distinct sample labels replicated to 250 rows with distinct filenames, the same replication scripts/measure.ts uses. Upload bytes are therefore representative; label VARIETY is not.
The rate limiter was not tripped once (0 of 250), which also exercises the shared guard added the same day under real batch load.
